question: Which 4.100.108 function implements LVGL v9 lv_image_set_src?
prototype_hypothesis: lv_image_set_src(image, src) sets the image source; dispatches on the source type (variable/pointer/file), validates the draw buffer, and invalidates the image cache.
callsite_evidence: sub_C3B2A5C decompiles to the canonical LVGL v9 lv_image_set_src and references "../../apps/graphics/lvgl/lvgl/src/widgets/image/lv_image.c" at lines 161 (unknown image type), 172 (failed to get image info), 184 (Invalid draw buffer)
It dispatches on the image header type byte (v4 from sub_C386CD8), sets the object's src pointer (offset +52), and invalidates via sub_C3ABE6C
The 'unknown image type' error uses the LVGL LV_LOG_ERROR convention with the source filename and function name as arguments
Produced by the multi-layer matcher from the verified 3.101.036 set and confirmed by decompiling the exact 4.100.108 IDB
The lv_image_* widget API confirms this firmware is LVGL v9 (v8 uses lv_img_set_src)
control_flow_evidence: On unknown source type (v4==3) it returns the object unchanged after logging 'unknown image type'
On a valid variable source it checks draw-buffer alignment (unaligned_data/handlers) before storing the source pointer
After setting the source it updates the object dirty/validity bytes (offset 96), recomputes layout (sub_C903EDC), and triggers a redraw (sub_C38222E) when dimensions differ
ownership_analysis: LVGL-owned: the image object owns the source pointer after set; callers must not free the source while the image is live. Runs on the LVGL owner thread.
unsafe_assumptions: The object field offsets (+52 src, +68/+72 size, +76/80/84, +96 flags) are the exact LVGL v9 layout in this IDB and are not portable
Callers must match the LVGL thread context (no concurrent lv_timer/lv_refr from another context)
recommended_probe: Create an image object, set a valid and an invalid source, and confirm the object renders and logs the expected error for the invalid case.
